name: theme-media-references-feedback-1
body:
source: review theme-library-refs/feedback-1 (target requirements.requirement.theme-media-references). The requirement body allowed an unprefixed relative theme-CSS reference to "stay inside the library root" (Guards: "a bare relative reference stays inside the library root"). Read literally that permits `url('../../slides/x/layout.html.tmpl')` or `url('../../library.yaml')` from `themes/a/theme.css` — files that exist (so load validation would pass) but that no route serves, so AC1 ("served and applied") fails. It also contradicted global.constraint.template-library-shareable (no references into `slides/`) and left open whether relative cross-tree reach (`../other/x.woff2`, `../../media/x`) is legal; such reach would make the `media:` / `theme:<name>/` prefixes redundant and relies on the served URL layout matching the library layout.

Resolution [autonomous]: restated the confinement per tree — an unprefixed relative reference resolves from the referencing file's own location and must stay inside that file's own tree (its theme directory, or `media/` for a stylesheet imported through `media:`); cross-tree reach happens ONLY through the reserved `media:` / `theme:<name>/` prefixes; no form may reference `slides/`, `sections/`, `library.yaml` or `AGENTS.md`. Added the AC case that rejects a relative `..` leaving its own tree with the offending CSS file and line (`url('../other/x.woff2')`, `url('../../slides/x/layout.html.tmpl')`, `url('../../library.yaml')` from a theme CSS — none resolves even though the target files exist). Propagated the same wording to requirements.requirement.templates-dir-validation (step 6 relative `url()`/`@import` confinement, plus the AC case), solution.component.template-library-loader and domain.value.media-asset. Coherence edit only to requirements.constraint.media-paths-library-relative (its "must stay inside the library root" sentence and the cross-tree sentence) so the requirement and its binding law agree; that constraint's separate review item theme-library-refs/feedback-2 is otherwise left to be routed on its own. Spine edges unchanged: theme-media-references still `contains`-from requirements.requirement.project-templates and still `drives` domain.entity.theme, domain.value.media-asset, domain.service.load-template-library and domain.service.template-registry.

Recovery caveat: while applying this fix, the requirement body was accidentally overwritten before it could be read. The pre-clobber body was subsequently recovered from git commit `f5081e4` (the last good state; the coordinator diffed it against the then-current state), and the three dropped pieces it revealed were restored verbatim: the Guards sentence naming the two embedded authoring guides and the agent-guide drift self-test (agent-authoring, library-agent-guide, agent-guide-drift-check); the serve-route sentence ("A stylesheet imported through `media:` is served and rewritten from the `media/` route; one imported through `theme:<name>/` is served and rewritten from that theme's route."); and the final AC bullet requiring both embedded guides to document both prefixes, drop the "theme reaches only its own directory" and "`media:` forbidden on `@import`" rules, and fail the agent-guide drift self-test when either prefix token is removed from BOTH guides. The node is therefore complete and matches the pre-clobber body, with the feedback-1 per-tree confinement wording retained; it is no longer merely a reconstruction.
